text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: page fired: routing-proxy-503-spike (group=rp-502-503, count=14) — targets: oncall@redwood.com. Auto-group id=grp-9832. Raw alert: HTTP 5xx spike > 10rps for 60s.

Maya: Acked. I'm on it. Seeing lots of duplicate PD pages.

Jordan S.: also acked. getting a lot of noisy alerts, looks like multiple group ids (grp-9832, grp-9833) for same upstream.

Samir R.: +1. PD is creating separate incidents because incident-bot grouping window is 10s. We should silence the PD rule to stop paging while we triage.

Maya: Can someone run a quick curl against /health on proxy frontends?

Jordan S.: running now — `curl -s -w "%{http_code}" -o /dev/null https://proxy-eu1.redwood/api/health` -> `504` from two hosts, 200s from others.

Lee: Looks like an upstream flapping issue. Could be autoscaler thrashing or a transient kube node network blip.

Samir R.: I'll temporarily silence the PagerDuty escalation for routing-proxy alerts for 15m. Use this PD API call if you need to remove sooner:
```bash
curl -X PUT "https://api.pagerduty.com/rules/routing-proxy/escalation-policy" \\  -H "Authorization: Token token=$PD_TOKEN" \\  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\  -d '{"escalation_policy": {"suppress_until": "2026-10-10T03:30:00Z"}}'
```

Maya: patched silence. Confirmed: PagerDuty shows suppressed for rule routing-proxy — no new pages for duplicates.

incident-bot: note: auto-group window currently 10s; incoming duplicates were split into multiple groups. Suggested config: `group_window: 60s` and `detection_threshold: >10rps` to reduce storms.

Jordan S.: I'm attaching a short log excerpt from proxy access logs (sensitive lines redacted):
```
[2026-10-10T03:05:21Z] proxy-eu1 ERR upstream_timeout service=svc-a host=10.10.3.12
[2026-10-10T03:05:22Z] proxy-eu2 ERR upstream_5xx service=svc-a host=10.10.3.13
[2026-10-10T03:05:23Z] proxy-eu1 WARN backend_reuse_failed service=svc-a
```

Samir R.: immediate mitigation steps I'm running: 1) cordon + drain node 10.10.3.12 (suspected NET), 2) scale svc-a from 3->5 replicas, 3) bump incident-bot group_window to 60s in staging config and rollfire.

Lee: If scaling reduces latency, we can keep suppression for another 10m and then test removing. Also we should avoid long silences for non-critical services.

Maya: FYI customer-impact: some in-flight requests to small subset of EU customers returned 5xx for ~2m. No data loss. Support ticket queue got 3 reports.

Jordan S.: pushing a canary config to incident-bot now — increase group window + enable dedupe_by: signature (endpoint+status) so identical alerts collapse.

incident-bot: deploy started: incident-bot:v2.14 -> rolling update (canary enabled).

Samir R.: Node cordon done. drain in progress. K8s events show `NetworkPlugin cni0 flapping` on node 10.10.3.12. If drain fails, we'll recycle kubelet.

Maya: I'm going to create a short runbook note in the incident ticket. Key actions: silence PD (15m), scale svc-a to 5, cordon node, apply group_window=60s in incident-bot canary, monitor 5xx rate.

Lee: Agree. Long-term action: update incident-bot housekeeping to: auto-group-window=60s, suppression_threshold=5 (suppress paging if >=5 duplicate alerts in 60s), and enable a cooldown per-group of 120s to avoid re-paging flaps. Add to infra backlog.

Jordan S.: Quick health check after scale: `kubectl get pods -l app=svc-a -o wide` shows new pods coming up healthy. 5xx rate dropping.

Maya: Good. I'm going to handoff to Lee in 30m. Leaving PD silence until 03:40Z. If anything spikes again, un-silence and page.

Samir R.: Note for ops: the auto-grouping algorithm also uses host IP and timestamp; that's why flapping caused multiple groups. We'll refactor to prefer signature-based grouping first.

incident-bot: automation note: auto-suppression applied to grp-9832, suppressed_id=supp-451.

Jordan S.: Confirmed 5xxs back down to baseline. Keeping watch.

Maya: Handoff: @Lee will be primary oncall from 03:35Z -> 07:00Z. Handoff checklist:
- PD silence expires at 03:40Z (check PD dashboard)
- Verify incident-bot canary rolled to 3/5 nodes before promoting
- Monitor support queue for any customer escalation
- If 5xx > baseline for 5m, escalate to infra pager (pagerduty:infra)

Lee: Taking handoff. I'll keep the suppression until we prove stability. If everything stays green by 04:30Z, I'll remove the silence and set the incident-bot group_window change to prod.

Maya: thanks — logging steps in the incident ticket and closing slack thread once resolved. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: incident grp-9832 status update: acknowledged by Maya, suppressed until 2026-10-10T03:40:00Z, escalations paused.

incident-bot: final note: filing a housekeeping task for automation team to add a paging-storm detector that auto-silences high-frequency dup alerts and creates one consolidated incident. Ticket created: INFRA-1543.

Lee: I'll follow up in INFRA-1543 and add acceptance criteria. Closing watch but staying available.
